self_forcing_rollout.What is exposure bias in autoregressive: Contrast the context each method conditions on during training (ground truth, noised ground truth, own outputs) with what inference conditions on. Cover how errors accumulate and why a video-level loss on the rollout addresses it.
self_forcing_rollout.Why does Self Forcing train a few-step d: Count the model calls one training rollout makes per block, and what unrolling and backpropagating through them would cost. Cover why a handful of steps keeps the sequential unroll affordable.
self_forcing_rollout.Self Forcing samples one exit step per i: Think about which step's input distribution gets a gradient in a given iteration, and what happens in expectation when the exit index is uniform. Cover what an early-exit output looks like.
self_forcing_rollout.Why is the cache entry computed under no: Separate two effects: graph memory kept across blocks, and which frames get gradient from a later frame's loss. Mention what the paper says it detaches, and where the context timestep and its small re-noise come from.

self_forcing_rollout.Self Forcing versus Diffusion Forcing fo: Cover parallel versus sequential training over frames, the special causal masks TF and DF need versus plain cached attention, what the paper reports on per-iteration time, and which training context matches inference.
self_forcing_rollout.Gradient truncation keeps memory bounded: Name the signals cut off: gradients through the cache into earlier blocks and through earlier denoising steps. Cover which dependencies that may hurt and options such as a longer differentiable window or recurrent state.
